newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Botswana sees 15th budget surplus in 1997/8.
newsitem.headline: Botswana sees 15th budget surplus in 1997/8.

text.p: Botswana should record its 15th consecutive budget surplus in 1997/98 (April-March) thanks to higher pula diamond revenues, vice president and finance minister Festus Mogae said on Friday.
"At this stage it looks like there will be a surplus (in 1997/8)," he said in an interview.
The fall in the pula meant that revenues from the country's pivotal diamond industry could be 10 to 15 percent higher when converted from dollars.
Mogae confirmed that the country now expected a budget surplus in 1996/7, after initially forecasting a 636 million pula shorftall, thanks to windfall pula profits on its dollar assets.
The pula has fallen by more than a fifth against the U.S. dollar since the beginning of the year as the authorities tracked the course of the ailing South African rand.
Mogae will present his 97/98 budget to parliament on February 10.
